R12-0.3 Decision needed from the owner (ledger L39)

        The AFCM re-implementation is not validated. H-R12 compares B2-S against AFCM.
        Possible routes (none taken):
               widen the λ_x grid below 1e-4 (the selection sat at its lower boundary);
               use Cui et al.’s quantile-transformed input;
               a REML-type smoothing selection;
               or run Round 12 with AFCM explicitly flagged as not validated.
        B2-S itself passed CK-5b, but only through ensemble averaging: each of the three members alone was above 0.10 for φ₁.


R12.1 Owner decisions (D120) and fact check

The owner’s four decisions are in D120 (R12.7), together with the operational details fixed before the runs. The fact check made five qualifications:

        The bivariate class is still not fully identified. Each channel’s curves span a 6-dimensional space, so x·c(t) with c outside that span still has no
        effect on η. This is why the projection in the identifiable RISE stays necessary.
        The new trend basis is not orthogonal to the Fourier sine terms. So the v2 covariance eigenfunctions are not the Fourier functions: CK-7
        stays on the Round-11 simulator, and PACE has no acceptance test under v2.
        Variance and signal changed. The time-averaged variance is unchanged at 1.875, but pointwise variance now ranges 1.09–2.59, and the SD of
        the true η rose from 0.45 to 0.71.
        A large λ_t removes curvature in t, not linear time variation, because of the second-order difference penalty.
        CK-11’s figures are as the owner stated them (n_test 400).


R12.2 What changed in the code

Module                                                                                  Change

kanfae.data.fsim                                                                        DGP “v2” (default) with level and trend terms; “v1” kept and pinned in every Round-11 test

R12.5 Why CK-6b failed (exploratory; not a test)

        Basis resolution is not the cause. The best possible fit of φ₁ within AFCM’s own x basis has a RISE far below 0.556:

x basis                                                                             Best possible RISE of φ₁ (approximation floor)

10 cubic B-splines on the training range (AFCM’s x basis)                           0.0020

15 on the training range                                                            0.0002

20 on the training range                                                            0.0000

10 on the 1st–99th percentile range of the test values                              0.0120


        So the error comes from estimation. Untested candidate explanations:
              the λ_x selection sits at the lower boundary of its grid;
              the time-constant φ₁ leaks into weakly identified bivariate directions, which the exact-null projection does not remove;
              AFCM is a single fit, whereas B2-S averages three.


R12.6 Gate decision

        Round 12 was not started. The owner’s rule requires all five repaired tests to pass; CK-6b failed.
        No Round-12 seed (3000–3419) was used, and nothing was run on real data.

R11-0.3 Decisions needed from the owner before Round 12

     1. S-Add identifiability (affects H-R12). Options, none taken:
                  a. keep the registration and report H-R12 with the caveat;
                  b. re-register RISE as error modulo the unidentified subspace;
                   c. re-register the DGP so that ∫X dt varies across subjects (for example, a random level per channel), and re-check identifiability before
                      any Round-12 seed is used.
     2. CK-3. The early-stopped linear-edge CoxKAN shrinks its slopes (max error 0.084 > 0.05). Decide whether the Cox-machinery check should compare
        at convergence (no early stopping), or whether this shrinkage is accepted as the training protocol’s property.
     3. CK-8. With θ_rel ≤ 0.10 nothing was pruned from the null channel. Decide whether the θ_rel grid, the functional edge score, or the expectation of
        the test should change.
     4. CK-11. The residual-calibrated model is calibrated (p 0.471). The Weibull model was only borderline miscalibrated (p 0.0515), so the contrast the
        test needs did not occur at this seed and n.

R11.2 What was implemented

Module                                                                                  Content

kanfae.survival.cox                                                                     Exact Breslow and Efron negative log partial likelihood (vectorised, differentiable, optional
                                                                                        strata); Breslow baseline; S(t | x)

kanfae.data.fsim                                                                        Round-12 simulator: S-Add, S-Int, S-Misspec (log-normal, log-logistic); dense or sparse (3–8
                                                                                        visits) curves; censoring calibrated to about 30%

kanfae.functional.pace                                                                  PACE (local linear mean and covariance, leave-one-subject-out bandwidths, σ² by a local
                                                                                        quadratic perpendicular to the diagonal, conditional-expectation scores)
Module                                                                            Content

kanfae.models.fkan                                                                B2-H, B2-S (rank 2), B2-deep; static heads (B1, static CoxKAN / KAN-AFT); Cox or AFT loss;
                                                                                  residual calibration; pruning grid; 3-seed ensemble with lr × weight-decay tuning; symbolic
                                                                                  stages 1–3 per edge in original units, substitution and refit

kanfae.models.afcm                                                                Additive functional Cox model (10 × 10 tensor cubic B-splines, second-order difference
                                                                                  penalties, 5 × 5 validation grid)

kanfae.models.lme                                                                 Random-intercept-and-slope LME by EM, BLUPs, two-stage LME + Cox

kanfae.models.fbaselines                                                          B1-SUM summaries, last values, dense grid FPCA, linear Cox for fpca_cox / sum_cox /
                                                                                  landmark_cox

kanfae.data.landmark                                                              B3 stacked landmark data set (history window, at-risk set, administrative censoring at the
                                                                                  horizon)


The deviations from the reference software and the operational choices are listed in D116 (R11.6).

R11.4 Why the failing tests failed

CK-5 and CK-6 (shape recovery): an identifiability defect in the design, plus estimation error.

        In S-Add, X_d(t) = 0.5·d·t + Σ_k ξ_dk ψ_k(t), and every Fourier ψ_k integrates to 0 over [0, 1]. So ∫X_d(t)dt is the same number for every subject.
        Consequence: adding c·x to φ_d (homogeneous case) adds the same constant to every subject’s η. The Cox likelihood cannot see that. In the
        bivariate case the same holds for x·c(t) whenever c(t) lies outside the span of the curves’ variation.
        The registered RISE removes per-t constants but not these linear-in-x parts, so it penalises a direction that the data cannot determine.

Development seed 902, n 2,000 (scripts/diag_round11_identifiability.py). Rank = number of singular values of the column-centred design above 1e-2 /
1e-3 / 1e-4 of the largest.

S-Add                             SD over subjects of ∫X_d dt     SD of the true ∫φ_d term           AFCM 10 × 10 design rank              Homogeneous design rank

channel 1                         1.4e-16                         0.228                              53 / 70 / 78 of 100                   8 / 8 / 8 of 10

channel 2                         1.7e-16                         0.173                              48 / 66 / 75 of 100                   8 / 8 / 8 of 10


Exploratory check (not a registered test; determinism check: the registered RISE values were reproduced exactly). “RISE-aff” removes the
best per-t affine function of x from the error. That removes more than the unidentified part, so it is optimistic.

Model (data)                      φ₁ RISE (registered)            φ₁ RISE-aff                        φ₂ RISE (registered)                  φ₂ RISE-aff

B2-S Cox ensemble (CK-5 data,     0.146                           0.139                              0.686                                 0.059
seed 12)

AFCM (CK-6 data, seed 13)         0.615                           0.538                              1.095                                 0.050


        For φ₂, almost all of the registered RISE is the linear-in-x part.
        For φ₁, it is not: B2-S still has RISE-aff 0.139 and AFCM 0.538.
        The two rows come from different seeds (12 and 13), so they are not a comparison between the methods.

CK-3.

        The slopes stopped at epoch 294, when validation patience ran out, short of the partial-likelihood maximum.
        Early stopping acts as shrinkage: all three slopes are smaller in absolute value than lifelines’.
        On development seeds 905 and 907 the same training loop ran until patience as well and came within 0.0003 of lifelines. So the outcome depends
        on the data seed.

CK-8.

        At λ ≤ 1e-3 no edge scored below θ_rel 0.10, the largest value in the registered grid, so nothing was pruned.
        At λ 1e-2, three edges were pruned, but every channel kept at least one edge.
        Selection picked λ 1e-4 with nothing pruned (validation losses tied across θ; the tie rule takes the largest θ).

CK-11. The test needs both “residual-calibrated p > 0.05” and “Weibull p < 0.05”. The first held (0.471); the second did not (0.0515).


R11.5 Before Round 12

        No Round-12 seed was used and nothing was run on real data.
        The decisions listed in §R11-0.3 are the owner’s.
        Until then, the code is ready for Round 12 except for these open items, and the identifiability finding (D118) should be resolved before H-R12 is
        computed.

R10-0.2 What the review changed in the plan

     1. The direct competitor is AFCM, not a strawman.
               Cui et al.’s model already uses ∫F(X(s), s)ds with penalised tensor-product splines under the Cox loss.
               A single-layer functional CoxKAN is that model with a different parametrisation and training procedure.
               The primary test therefore compares shape recovery against AFCM (H-R12), not against a linear model.
     2. Every published KAN survival model uses static covariates. CoxKAN, KAN-AFT, SurvKAN and KAPLAN all do. Their “time-varying” features
        concern effects that change with time, not covariates measured over time.
     3. Two pieces of closely related work could only be checked at abstract level.
               JM-KAN (a KAN joint model with yearly landmarks; conference abstract).
               F-KAN (FPC scores → KAN for a scalar response).
               Their full texts are needed before any “first” wording.
     4. No R in this environment. AFCM and the joint-model-style baseline will be Python re-implementations with their own acceptance tests (CK-6, CK-
        12), disclosed as deviations from mgcv/JM.

R10.1 Owner decisions and fact check (D110)

        Framing. Functional CoxKAN / KAN-AFT (B1, B2, B3) is the main study; KAN-FAE (Rounds 1–9) is the motivating architectural section.
        Scope. Full scope as listed in D110: baselines, the four simulation scenarios with N = 20, the real data sets, and measured interpretability.
        Fact check. Every cited work exists as named. The AFCM model form is as stated. aids and prothro are in JM 1.5-2 (prothro’s documentation is
        internally inconsistent: 488 vs 467 patients). CoxKAN’s own loss approximates ties, so our exact Efron/Breslow implementation is a disclosed
        deviation. R is unavailable, so AFCM and the joint-model-style baseline will be re-implemented.


R10.2 Literature review

Literature review, Round 10 (2026-10-19): functional and longitudinal survival models, KAN survival models

Scope and method. This is a targeted review, not a systematic one: no database protocol, no screening log, no double screening. It extends the round-2
review (docs/literature_review.md, kept unchanged). The questions are those the owner set in D110:

        What exists for survival analysis with functional or longitudinal covariates (functional linear Cox, additive functional Cox, joint models, landmarking,
        deep dynamic models)?
        What exists for KAN-based survival models?
        What exists for KAN-based functional regression?
        Where do the planned Functional CoxKAN / KAN-AFT models (B1, B2, B3) sit relative to all of these?

Each item was verified by a web search, its landing page, its arXiv abstract page, or Crossref metadata (api.crossref.org), as marked in the tables.
“Abstract” means only the abstract or metadata was read, so claims about methodological detail beyond it are not made. Search date: 2026-10-19.

R10.4 Design note and pre-registration of Rounds 11–13

Round 10 design note and pre-registration of Rounds 11–13 (2026-10-19)

Owner decisions: D110. Literature and claim policy: D111 (docs/literature_review_round10.md). Pre-registrations: D112 (Round 11), D113 (Round 12), D114
(Round 13). This document is the binding specification. Any change after the commit that registers it needs an owner-approved decision entry and is
reported as a deviation.

Notation.

      Subject i has D longitudinal channels X_id(t), observed at times t_ij (with noise) on a history window rescaled to [0, 1], scalar covariates z_i, and the
      outcome (Y_i, δ_i).
      G is a fixed grid of 50 equispaced points on [0, 1]. Integrals ∫·dt are trapezoid quadratures on G.
      In tests, X̂_id(·) denotes the reconstructed curve on G: smoother output (dense data) or PACE conditional expectation (sparse data).

1. Survival losses and the shared KAN machinery (Round 11)

      Cox (CoxKAN).
           η_i = f(·) (no intercept).
           Negative log partial likelihood with exact Breslow and Efron tie handling (both implemented; Efron is the default, as in lifelines).
           Breslow estimator of the baseline cumulative hazard Λ̂_0(t). Predicted survival S(t | x) = exp(−Λ̂_0(t) e^η).
           CoxKAN’s original fast approximation is not used; this is a documented deviation.
      AFT (KAN-AFT).
           log T = μ + η + σε.
           Losses already in the code base: parametric Weibull, IPCW, transform least squares, Buckley–James.
           New: non-parametric residual calibration. Survival is predicted as S(t | x) = Ŝ_ε((log t − μ̂ − η̂)/σ̂), with Ŝ_ε the Kaplan–Meier estimate of
           the standardised residuals on the training data. This is used for KAN-AFT under S-Misspec and for C-MAPSS.
      KAN layers.
           Existing B-spline KAN layer (kanfae.models.kan): grid 5, order 3, SiLU base.
           Inputs are standardised with training statistics, not BatchNorm, so that edge functions are readable in original units after back-
           transformation.
           Grid range: [−3, 3] in standardised units, plus an extension for out-of-range inputs.
      Regularisation and scale-aware pruning (replaces the absolute θ = 1e-2 rule; round 8 showed it prunes nothing on unit-scale inputs).
           Loss + λ·(|Φ|₁ + 2·S(Φ) + |C|₁).
           The edge score s_e = mean over training inputs of |φ_e − mean φ_e| (centred, D54), normalised as s̃_e = s_e / max_e’ s_e’ within the layer.
           An edge is pruned if s̃_e < θ_rel. A pruned edge’s mean is absorbed into the output bias.
           Grid: λ ∈ {0, 1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2} × θ_rel ∈ {0, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.10}.
           Procedure: train at each λ; prune at each θ_rel; fine-tune 200 epochs with the mask fixed.
           Selection by validation loss (Cox: validation negative log partial likelihood, Efron; AFT: the training loss on the validation split). Ties go to the
           larger θ_rel, then the larger λ.
           Channel selection: a channel is “selected” if any of its edges survives pruning.
      Symbolic extraction (kanfae.symbolic.fit):
           stage 1: linear;
           stage 2: library;
           stage 3: PySR.
           Acceptance: validation R² > 0.99.
           PySR (60 s per edge) runs only on edges carrying at least 5% of the layer’s total centred score, at most 10 per model.
           Metrics are reported before pruning, after pruning and after substitution.

2. Model families

B1: two-stage interpretable coordinates.

      B1-FPCA. FPCA scores per channel, with K_d chosen by 95% fraction of variance explained (max 5).
           Dense data: eigen-decomposition of the smoothed curves on G.
           Sparse data: PACE (Yao, Müller & Wang 2005), new module kanfae.functional.pace. Mean and covariance by local linear smoothing with a
           bandwidth chosen by leave-one-subject-out CV; scores by conditional expectation.
           The scores, together with z, feed:
                  a 1-layer additive KAN [p → 1] (B1-FPCA-1), or
                  a 2-layer KAN [p → 4 → 1] (B1-FPCA-2);
                  under the Cox loss (CoxKAN) or AFT loss (KAN-AFT).
           Effect curves in X are recovered as φ_d(·) composed with the eigenfunctions (reported as β-type functions).
      B1-SUM. Per channel:
           the level (last value before the landmark, and the mean);
           the slope (OLS);
           the variability (residual SD).
           These feed the same KAN heads.
B2: functional KAN layer on X(t), new module kanfae.models.fkan.

        B2-H (time-homogeneous): η = Σ_d ∫₀¹ φ_d(X̂_d(t)) dt + Σ_k ψ_k(z_k). Each φ_d and ψ_k is a univariate KAN edge.
        B2-S (separable bivariate, rank M = 2): φ_d(x, t) = Σ_{m=1..M} g_dm(x)·h_dm(t). Each g and h is a univariate KAN edge (h on t ∈ [0, 1]). The
        learned surface and its symbolic form are read in x and t separately.
        B2-deep (for interactions):
              Functional summaries s_dm = ∫ g_dm(X̂_d(t)) h_dm(t) dt feed a second KAN layer [D·M + p → 4 → 1].
        Input scale.
              Primary: X̂ standardised by the training mean and SD pooled over G, then back-transformed for plots and formulas.
              Sensitivity: the pointwise quantile transform x̃(t) = F̂_t(X̂(t)) of Cui et al.
        Identifiability.
              Each φ_d is centred: E over training (i, t) of φ_d = 0, with the constant absorbed in the baseline.
              For B2-S, g and h are rescaled after training so that ||h_dm||₂ = 1.
        Losses. Cox (Efron) or AFT (parametric Weibull primary; residual-calibrated variant).
        Training. Adam, lr {1e-3, 3e-3} × weight decay {1e-4, 1e-3} tuned on validation loss; early stopping with patience 100; maximum 3,000 epochs;
        the 3-seed ensemble (seeds 0–2) is the primary prediction.
        Ensemble shapes. Shape estimates are the mean of the members’ centred φ̂, which is valid because η is additive in φ.

B3: stacked landmark supermodel (real data, Round 13).

        Landmarks t_L on a pre-registered grid per data set (§5).
        For each subject at risk at t_L: features from history up to t_L only (B1-SUM, B1-FPCA/PACE, or B2 on the window [t_L − W, t_L]). The outcome is
        time since the landmark, administratively censored at horizon w.
        The stacked data set has one row per (subject, landmark).
        Model: CoxKAN with a landmark-stratified baseline, and t_L also entering as a KAN edge input, so that effects can vary with the landmark
        (supermodel).
        Splits are by subject. Evaluation uses time-dependent AUC and Brier score at t_L + w, and C within the horizon, per landmark.

4. Simulation study (Round 12): data-generating processes

Common to all scenarios.

        n = 1,000 subjects (train/validation/test 60/20/20, the existing split_groups), D = 3 channels on t ∈ [0, 1].
        Curves: X_d(t) = μ_d(t) + Σ_{k=1..4} ξ_dk ψ_k(t), with ψ_k orthonormal Fourier functions, ξ_dk ~ N(0, λ_k), λ = (1, 0.5, 0.25, 0.125), and μ_d(t) =
        0.5·d·t.
        Observations X_d(t_ij) + N(0, 0.2²).
               Dense: 40 equispaced times.
               Sparse (S-Sparse only): 3–8 visits (uniform count) at uniform random times.
        Scalar covariates: z_1 ~ N(0, 1) (linear effect 0.3), z_2 ~ Bernoulli(0.5) (effect −0.3).
        Censoring: independent uniform, calibrated per scenario to about 30%.
        Truth is stored in the oracle for every subject.

Replicates and seeds (verified unused on 2026-10-19):

        N = 20 per scenario.
        S-Add 3000–3019; S-Int 3100–3119; S-Sparse 3200–3219; S-Misspec 3300–3319 (each seed generates both sub-scenarios from independent
        streams); S-Int/P0 continuity 3400–3419.
Models per scenario.

      S-Add, S-Sparse: B2-H, B2-S (Cox and AFT); B1-FPCA-1 (Cox, AFT); B1-SUM; afcm; fpca_cox; sum_cox; sum_rsf; static_coxkan.
             S-Sparse adds the PACE front end for B1/B2 against the fixed B-spline front end, and flat_ae.
      S-Int: the above, plus B1-FPCA-2 and B2-deep.
      S-Int/P0: fae_kan_s3 vs fae_mlp_s3 only.
      S-Misspec: CoxKAN vs KAN-AFT (parametric Weibull; residual-calibrated) for B2-S, plus afcm.

Metrics.

      Survival: survival-curve error against the oracle, IBS (marginal IPCW), Harrell C, Uno C (τ = 90% quantile), D-calibration p.
      Shape (S-Add, S-Sparse, S-Misspec): relative ISE:
            RISE_d = ∫∫ (φ̂_d^c − φ_d^c)² w_d dx dt / ∫∫ (φ_d^c)² w_d dx dt, with the superscript c denoting centring and w_d the empirical density of
            (X_d(t), t) in the test data.
            Homogeneous effects integrate over x only.
            For Cox, φ is identified up to a constant (centring). For AFT, the comparison uses −φ̂/σ̂-scaled shapes against the PH-equivalent truth only in
            S-Add, and the AFT truth in S-Misspec.
            Primary shape summary: the mean RISE over the active channels (1, 2).
      Selection: recall of the active channels {1, 2} and the false discovery rate (null channel 3 selected), from pruning.
      Symbolic: acceptance rate and validation R² of edges; formula RISE after substitution.

Statistical analysis.

      Paired over replicates; mean difference, SD, 95% t-CI (df 19), paired-t p, exact Wilcoxon p, sign counts.
      Single confirmatory test of Round 12 (H-R12):
            Quantity: in S-Add, B2-S under the Cox loss (functional CoxKAN) minus afcm in mean RISE over the active channels.
            Test: two-sided paired t-test, α = 0.05, N = 20.
            Interpretation, fixed now:
                   If the 95% CI lies entirely below 0, B2-S recovers shapes better than AFCM.
                   If it lies entirely above 0, worse.
                   If it lies inside ±0.05 (absolute RISE), the two are declared equivalent within the margin (TOST at α = 0.05 each side).
                   Otherwise, inconclusive.
      Pre-registered secondary tests (exploratory, no multiplicity correction):
            S-Add survival-curve error, B2-S vs afcm.
            B2-S vs B1-FPCA-1 (RISE).
            Selection recall/FDR.
            S-Int: B2-deep vs B2-S, and B1-FPCA-2 vs B1-FPCA-1 (curve error).
            S-Int/P0 continuity: TOST equivalence of fae_kan_s3 vs fae_mlp_s3 in survival-curve error, margin ±0.005 (about 5% of the round-9 MLP S3
            error, 0.0915). This re-confirms the round-9 F1 finding with fixed criteria on fresh seeds.
            S-Sparse: PACE vs fixed B-spline front end (RISE, curve error); flat_ae vs B2.
            S-Misspec: KAN-AFT (residual-calibrated) vs CoxKAN (curve error, D-calibration).
      Every run is reported. Failed fits are recorded and counted.

Real-data protocol.

      5 outer splits by subject (seeds 0–4) and the same models as S-Add, with lme2_cox and landmark_cox added.
      Metrics: IBS (marginal and conditional IPCW), Harrell and Uno C, D-calibration; for B3, time-dependent AUC and Brier per landmark.
      KAN vs reference comparisons use the Nadeau–Bengio corrected t-interval.
      C-MAPSS: KAN-AFT with residual calibration (the calibration fix) against round 1’s parametric AFT; D-calibration reported.

Interpretability deliverables (pre-registered measures).

      Stability: for each selected effect, the centred φ̂_d across the 5 outer splits × 20 bootstrap resamples of the training split. Report the mean
      pairwise R² and mean pairwise cosine similarity on a common x-grid (the 5th–95th percentile of pooled X).
      Effect plots with bootstrap 90% bands, in original clinical units.
      Clinical alignment. Directions fixed now, from established clinical knowledge:
            PBC: higher bilirubin increases risk; higher albumin decreases risk; longer prothrombin time increases risk.
            prothro: a lower prothrombin index increases risk.
            aids: a lower CD4 count increases risk.
            An effect “aligns” if its centred φ̂ is monotone in the stated direction over the 5th–95th percentile range in at least 80% of the split ×
            bootstrap fits.
      Symbolic formulas in original units for accepted edges, reported with validation R².

6. Round 11 acceptance tests (unit tests written before any Round-12/13 run)

Thresholds are fixed now. A STAT test failure at its pre-specified seed is recorded as FAIL and is never converted by changing the seed, sample size or
threshold.
ID                                                   Type                                               Criterion

                                                                                                        lifelines (Efron) and a direct Breslow formula, for fixed

                                                                                                        reproduces ∫X(t)dt for analytic curves within 1e-3

                                                                                                        RISE < 0.10 (n = 2,000, seed 13)

CK-7                                                 STAT                                               PACE on sparse curves (3–8 visits) recovers the first
                                                                                                        eigenfunction with |cosine| > 0.95 and reconstructs curves
                                                                                                        with lower mean ISE than per-subject B-spline smoothing (n
                                                                                                        = 1,000, seed 14)

CK-8                                                 STAT                                               Scale-aware pruning with validation-selected (λ, θ_rel)
                                                                                                        removes the null channel and keeps both active channels in
                                                                                                        S-Add (n = 2,000, seed 15)

CK-9                                                 DET                                                The stacked landmark builder uses no observation after t_L,
                                                                                                        includes only subjects at risk at t_L, and censors at t_L + w

CK-10                                                DET                                                Symbolic stages 1–2 recover sin, tanh and quadratic edges
                                                                                                        with validation R² > 0.99

CK-11                                                STAT                                               The residual-calibrated KAN-AFT has D-calibration p > 0.05
                                                                                                        on log-normal AFT data where the Weibull-loss AFT has p <
                                                                                                        0.05 (n = 2,000, seed 16)

CK-12                                                DET                                                The two-stage LME’s BLUPs equal closed-form BLUPs for
                                                                                                        known variance components within 1e-8


Unit-test seeds 11–16 are training/data seeds for tests only (never used for Round 12/13 data).

7. Compute budget and order

        Round 12: about 5 scenarios × 20 replicates × about 12 models × 3 training seeds, single-threaded, 4 parallel lanes. Planning budget: 12 h wall
        clock.
        If the budget is exceeded, these cells are dropped first, in this order:
               B2 quantile sensitivity;
               S-Misspec log-logistic;
               flat_ae;
               sum_rsf.
        H-R12 cells (S-Add B2-S Cox and afcm) are never dropped.
        Round 13: 4 data sets × 5 splits; the bootstrap stability analysis (20 resamples) only for the selected B2 and B1 models.

8. Known limitations accepted at registration

        AFCM and the joint-model baseline are Python re-implementations (no R), so differences from mgcv/JM are possible.
        Dynamic-DeepHit and JM-KAN are not implemented.
        n = 1,000 synthetic subjects; three channels only.
        The clinical-alignment directions are coarse (monotonicity).
        Clinical sign-off for PBC endpoints is external.

R9-0.1 Outcome

Item                                                                                      Result

L32 decision 1: KAN-fairness study (D108; P0, replicates 1000–1004; 10 cells, 400 runs,   Run. Under tuned S3 the KAN–MLP survival gap vanishes (F1: curve error −0.0001, 95% CI
all completed)                                                                            [−0.0030, +0.0028]). Removing the decoder bottleneck does not close the gap under S2
                                                                                          (F2, F3) and does not help under S3. In no arm or strategy is KAN-FAE better than the
                                                                                          MLP on survival

Item                                                                                        Result

Ledger L32                                                                                  Closed (D107–D109)


R9-0.2 What we learned

   1. The round-8 H1 deficit is a training-strategy effect.
            With reconstruction pre-training (S3), tuned, the KAN encoder matches the MLP on survival: curve error, IBS, Harrell C and Uno C differences
            are all ≈ 0 with CIs straddling 0.
            This holds with the D31 decoder and with an unbottlenecked KAN decoder.
   2. The decoder bottleneck is not what held KAN back on survival.
            Under S2, removing it narrows the curve-error gap from +0.0078 to about +0.005 but does not close it.
            Under S3, swapping in the MLP decoder makes KAN slightly worse (+0.006, 5/5).
   3. The bottleneck does limit reconstruction, strongly.
            KAN’s test reconstruction error is 0.31–0.53 with the width-3 decoder, against 0.12–0.16 with either unbottlenecked decoder.
            This is consistent with the owner’s hypothesis for the S1 collapse (round 8). The survival head does not depend on reconstruction quality
            here.
   4. S3 helps every architecture. It lowers curve error by 0.006–0.016 in all five arms, most for KAN.
   5. No configuration shows a KAN advantage. The best survival cells (C 0.864–0.868; curve error 0.091–0.093) include both KAN and MLP arms
      and are indistinguishable at n = 5.

fae_mlp_wide (hidden 107)                                         MLP 32→107→16                  MLP 16→107→36                 10966


Modes.

        Mode B keeps the exact C4F KAN encoder (its initialisation is bit-identical) and gives it fae_mlp’s decoder architecture. It is decoder-matched; its
        encoder + decoder total is 30% larger than fae_mlp’s (disclosed).
        Mode A replaces the D31 decoder with a single KAN layer 16 → 36, so no hidden width is below r. It is compared with an MLP whose hidden width
        (107) matches its encoder + decoder parameters (+0.3%).
Protocol. Every arm uses C4F and protocol 2.1 tuning (lr × wd at seed 0, by validation IBS). The primary result per replicate is the 3-seed ensemble on
test. Test reconstruction error is the individual-weighted MSE of the objective-state model on the observed test points, averaged over members.

Tests. FC-1..FC-5 were written and passed before any fairness fit. A first run failed on a construction error in FC-2’s setup; it is kept in the records.

Reading.

     Reconstruction improves strongly. Giving the KAN encoder the MLP’s decoder lowers its reconstruction error (−0.16 under S2, −0.40 under S3,
     5/5).

     0. Under S3 it is even slightly worse than the bottlenecked KAN.

     parameters than fae_mlp.

R9.7 PBC endpoint (L32 decision 3)

Endpoints. E2 (death or liver transplantation; transplant-free survival) remains the primary reported PBC endpoint, and E1 (death, transplantation
censored) the sensitivity analysis. The supervising professor’s clinical sign-off is outside the codebase.
What does and does not depend on the choice. Every PBC model comparison in this project reaches the same conclusion under both endpoints: no
detectable difference. This covers KAN-AFT vs linear AFT (round 2) and fae_kan vs fae_mlp (round 8). The point estimates are not identical, and some
change sign. So the invariance is claimed for the conclusions only.

R8-0.2 What we learned

   1. The conventional baseline finally qualifies.
            A nonlinear risk head on the r = 16 representation, with risk averaged over three training seeds, passed the gate on fresh seed 93 and 5/5
            fresh confirmations.
            It would also have passed under round 7’s stricter criteria, so the verdict does not rest on the round-8 relaxations.
   2. H1 (primary): no KAN advantage.
            On P0, KAN-FAE has slightly higher survival-curve error than the parameter-matched MLP-FAE: +0.0078, 95% CI [+0.0002, +0.0155], worse
            on 5/5 replicates. IBS points the same way.
            By the protocol this is weak evidence that the KAN encoder is worse under this configuration. It is not evidence of an advantage.
   3. The pattern repeats elsewhere.
            fae_kan is worse than fae_mlp in every secondary synthetic setting and on C-MAPSS (Harrell C −0.021, Nadeau–Bengio CI excludes 0).
            On PBC the two are indistinguishable.
   4. H2: reconstruction did not help survival. α = 1 vs α = 0 makes no detectable difference, and the AB1 α sweep (0–10) is flat.
   5. H3 is reversed. Under sparse sampling the flattened autoencoder has lower curve error than both functional autoencoders (−0.014 vs fae_mlp,
      5/5 replicates).
   6. Training strategy matters more than the encoder family.
            Reconstruction pre-training followed by joint training (S3) is best for both encoders (C 0.867 / 0.866), and under S3 the KAN–MLP gap
            disappears.
            A linear encoder block (AB3) does as well as either nonlinear one: the frequency-aware front does the nonlinear work.
   7. KAN pruning removes almost nothing, and symbolic substitution changes nothing.
            At the reference threshold, pruning removes 0–1 of 512 risk-encoder edges; survival metrics are unchanged and reconstruction gets worse.
            Symbolic formulas replace 56% of the risk-encoder edges with no loss. But they map abstract front features to latent units, so they are not
            interpretable risk formulas.

R8-0.3 What this does and does not show

       Statistical strength. Five replicates, and one pre-registered primary test (p = 0.047). Everything else is exploratory, with no correction for
       multiplicity.
       H1 is conditional on C4F. C4F was selected and gated for the MLP. The KAN arm shares it (as the protocol requires) and, to stay parameter-
       matched at r = 16, carries a width-3 decoder bottleneck. The S3 control shows the KAN deficit can vanish under another training strategy. H1
       therefore says “not better under the MLP-selected configuration”, not “KAN cannot help”.
       How the gate criteria evolved. They were relaxed over rounds 5–8, every change disclosed. 4f passes the round-7 set as well; the strict round-5
       margin (0.015) would fail it on the gate seed.
       Real data. PBC E2 is still a provisional endpoint. C-MAPSS calibration is poor for both neural arms (D-calibration p ≈ 0). The neural arms are not
       better than the round-1 comparators on either data set.
       Symbolic formulas describe single encoder edges on abstract features, so they do not add interpretability at the level of the curve parameters or
       covariates.

         Selection. The jointly trained nonlinear head gives the best single-seed and ensemble validation C. Its latent probes are slightly lower but within

Reading.

        Pruning finds almost nothing to remove. The KAN encoder’s edges are not small at θ = 1e-2, because BatchNorm makes every input unit-
        scale. Sparsity regularisation (λ = 1e-3) did not change that for the risk path. It did make the objective-state encoder more fragile: reconstruction
        after pruning degrades from 0.32 to 0.51–0.58.
        Substitution is behaviour-preserving but not explanatory. About 56% of edges have an accurate library formula (validation R² > 0.99), and
        swapping them in leaves every survival metric unchanged. Each edge maps one abstract front feature to one latent unit, and the risk then passes
        through an MLP head. No compact formula for risk in terms of the curve parameters results.

                                                                                       regularisation (λ 1e-3) survival is unchanged and
                                                                                       post-pruning reconstruction degrades strongly
                                                                                       (0.320 → 0.577 / 0.506). Symbolic (replicate
                                                                                       1000, risk-state encoder): stages 1–2
                                                                                       accepted 852/1529 edges (plain) and 805/1481
                                                                                       (regularised), almost all library formulas; PySR
                                                                                       accepted 7 of the 10 highest-L1 rejected edges;
                                                                                       test metrics after substitution are unchanged (C
                                                                                       0.8584 → 0.8588). The formulas map abstract
                                                                                       front features to latent units; they are not
                                                                                       formulas in the curve parameters or covariates,
                                                                                       and the risk head is an MLP. Real data: PBC
                                                                                       E2/E1, fae_kan − fae_mlp: Nadeau–Bengio CIs
                                                                                       wide and include 0 for every metric; both are
                                                                                       comparable to the round-1 comparators (E2 C
                                                                                       0.829 vs 0.824–0.846). C-MAPSS FD001 Option B:
                                                                                       fae_kan worse than fae_mlp (Harrell C −0.021,
                                                                                       NB CI [−0.035, −0.008], 5/5). fae_mlp is
                                                                                       comparable to the comparators (C 0.863 vs
                                                                                       0.860–0.865) but not better in RUL RMSE (37.9 vs
                                                                                       34.2–37.2), and both neural arms have D-
                                                                                       calibration p ≈ 0. Caveats: n = 5; one primary
                                                                                       test; everything else exploratory, without
                                                                                       multiplicity correction. C4F was selected for
                                                                                       fae_mlp, and fae_kan shares it (protocol design),
                                                                                       with a D31-forced decoder bottleneck of width 3.
                                                                                       So H1 is conditional on the MLP-selected
                                                                                       configuration, and the S3 control shows the gap
                                                                                       can vanish under another training strategy.

R8.14 Reproducibility

Reproducibility

Project instructions (the repository README.md is intentionally left unchanged, D28).
### environment (project-local; never touches the global Python)
bash scripts/setup_env.sh                          # or: KANFAE_FROM_LOCK=1 bash scripts/setup_env.sh
bash scripts/verify_env.sh                         # E-1 / E-5 evidence
### tests (every attempt is appended to reports/logs/test_records.jsonl)
KANFAE_RUN_ID=rerun .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -rA tests/
### data (public sources; checksums in reports/run_manifest.json)
###   C-MAPSS: https://phm-datasets.s3.amazonaws.com/NASA/6.+Turbofan+Engine+Degradation+Simulation+Data+Set.zip
###            -> extract inner CMAPSSData.zip into data/raw/cmapss/

R7-0.2 What we learned

   1. The representation problem is solved.
            With latent size r = 16, the latent encodes all four curve parameters on every fresh seed: test probe means 0.83–0.88, ω 0.85–0.92.
            It passes even the strictest probe definition used so far (mean ≥ 0.80) on all six fresh seeds. The re-referenced probe threshold (0.75)
            therefore decided nothing.
   2. Patience was not the lever; capacity was.
            Patience 300 gave fits identical to patience 100: the joint objective had no later minimum.
            Raising r from 12 to 16 lifted the weakest training seed’s probe from 0.779 to 0.829.
   3. The remaining gap is concordance relative to C_ceiling.
            Across the six fresh test splits, C − C_ceiling lies between −0.008 and −0.022. Two splits (seeds 92, 143) fall just beyond the 0.020 margin.
            On seed-92 validation, five training seeds give C − C_ceiling between −0.014 and −0.021, with a training-seed SD of 0.0026.
            So the 0.0022 shortfall is within training-seed variation. The systematic part (about −0.016) is the gap between a linear AFT head on the
            latent and the nonlinear true risk formula, which C_ceiling applies.
   4. R3 failed in an unexpected direction. Censoring awareness works: the censoring-aware error is about half the naive one on all three training
      seeds. But R3 also requires |C_censored − C_R2| ≤ 0.02, and here C on the censored data (0.8638) exceeded R2’s C (0.8384) by 0.0254.

R7-0.3 Decision requested (nothing has been run)

Seeds 92 and 141–145 are now used; any further gate needs new fresh seeds.

   1. (Recommended) Revision 4f: the risk mapping.
            Keep the 4e representation fixed.
            Pre-register a Step-1 search on seed-21 validation over two factors:
                   the risk head: linear (current) vs a small nonlinear head on the latent;
                   averaging the risk score over training seeds 0–2.
            Rationale: these target the two measured parts of the gap, the head’s approximation error (about −0.016) and single-seed variance (SD
            0.0026). D74’s negative result for an MLP head was obtained on the much weaker 4b latent, so it needs re-testing.
   2. R3’s form (your call, prospectively only).
            R3 is two-sided, so it fails when censored-data concordance is better than R2’s.
            A one-sided form (C_censored ≥ C_R2 − 0.02) would match its stated purpose. It would have passed on seed 92, which is exactly why it can
            only be adopted for new seeds.
   3. Or accept the verdict. The MLP stays not gate-qualified, and H1 stays blocked.

H1 stays blocked under every option until a gate is passed.

Reading.

        The concordance shortfall is within training-seed noise. The gate fits one training seed (0). Across seeds 0–4, validation C varies with SD
        0.0026, more than the 0.0022 shortfall.
        The gap to C_ceiling is systematic. It averages about −0.016 on this split and −0.008 to −0.022 across the six fresh test splits. C_ceiling applies
        the true nonlinear risk formula to per-individual parameter estimates; the model uses a linear AFT head on the latent. With the latent now encoding
        the parameters well, this head gap is the most plausible remaining source.
        R3. The censored-data model’s C (0.8638) exceeds R2’s single fit (0.8384), so the symmetric tolerance fails. R3’s purpose (censoring awareness) is

R6-0.2 What we learned

   1. The survival side is now solved and stable. Every candidate on every training seed reaches validation C 0.84–0.85, the level of the data-
      attainable reference, with zero loss spikes.
   2. The stopping rule is no longer the issue.
            Within a learning rate, all two-state rules and burn-ins give identical latents (and so identical probes).
            The latent always comes from the joint-objective minimum. The stopping rule only chooses which state supplies risk.
   3. The binding constraint is the representation’s linear encoding of b and A.
            The probe for the x₁ slope b is 0.68–0.78, and for the amplitude A 0.73–0.84.
            Training seed 1 is weakest (b 0.676, A 0.725).
            The lower learning rate improves the latent (minimum seed probe 0.753 → 0.779; minimum ω 0.666 → 0.813), but not enough.
   4. The 0.001 shortfall is not waived. Relaxing a threshold after seeing the result would be a post-hoc change. The rule was applied as registered.

R6-0.3 Decision requested (nothing has been run)

The evidence points at the representation, not the stopping rule. Two clean options:

   1. (Recommended) A pre-registered representation-capacity step, with the same multi-seed rule and fresh seeds, and lr 1e-3 with two-
      checkpoint stopping fixed:
            the latent size r ∈ {12, 16};
            the objective patience ∈ {100, 300}, letting reconstruction, and with it the b and A encoding, keep improving before the objective minimum
            is taken.
   2. An explicit owner override, recorded as a protocol deviation: send the closest candidate (two-checkpoint, lr 1e-3, burn-in 300) to the fresh gate
      despite its 0.001 shortfall on one seed.

H1 stays blocked either way until the MLP passes a pre-registered gate.

R6.4 Why Step 1 failed

        Probes are identical across stopping modes. Within each learning rate, all four stopping modes and burn-ins produce exactly the same latent
        probes. The latent is the joint-objective-minimum state (epochs 442–1076), which these settings do not alter. They change only the risk state
        (validation C 0.839–0.850).
        b and A are the weak components. The slope b of x₁ (0.68–0.78) and the amplitude A (0.73–0.84) are what pull the probe mean down.
        Frequency ω meets its threshold at lr 1e-3 (≥ 0.813).
        The decisive cell. At lr 1e-3, training seed 1 (b 0.676, A 0.725) gives a probe mean of 0.779, short of 0.78 by 0.001.
        Next lever: the remaining gap is representational, so further progress must come from the representation (capacity, or longer reconstruction
        training before the objective minimum), not from stopping (§R6-0.3).

R5-0.2 What we learned

    1. Instability fixed.
             Balancing the spectral path to the A3 path and clipping gradients removed the loss spikes: in full 3000-epoch runs, jumps fell from 12
             (maximum training NLL 12.5) to 0 (maximum 1.14).
             The run-to-run spread across thread counts fell from 0.013 to 0.0006.
    2. Concordance gap closed. With stable training and survival-optimal stopping, test C now reaches the amended, data-attainable reference on the
       gate seed (0.8421 ≥ 0.8390). Three of five confirmation seeds come within about 0.006 of it.
    3. The latent is now the failure.
             Stopping at the survival optimum (validation NLL minimum, epochs 91–430) ends training before the latent has learned b and A (probe b
             0.57–0.67).
             On one seed (135), the validation NLL dipped at epoch 91 and the whole model was undertrained.
    4. A disclosed tie-break decided this. At search step H3, NLL early stopping and the two-checkpoint rule gave identical risk predictions. The
       registered tie-break kept the simpler single-state rule, whose latent is earlier and weaker. The two-checkpoint rule’s latent (from the objective
       minimum) had a higher validation probe (0.818 vs 0.787). It was not gate-tested: that would be a post-hoc look.
    5. Determinism.
             The 0.0053 difference between Tables R4.3 and R4.5a comes from thread-count-dependent floating point, amplified by the instability: 3
             threads were even non-deterministic between two identical runs.
             All round-5 fits are single-threaded and reproducible (R5.1).

R5-0.3 Recommended next step (owner decision; nothing has been run)

Pre-register two-checkpoint stopping with a minimum training period. The representation trains to the joint-objective minimum; risk is taken from
the validation-NLL minimum, but only over epochs ≥ a burn-in (for example 300), so that an early transient dip cannot end training.

Choose it by robustness across training seeds (seeds 0–2 on validation), not seed 0 alone. Then evaluate on a new fresh gate seed and new
confirmation seeds under the D82 criteria, which stay unchanged.

H1 stays blocked until then.

R5.1 Determinism and the 0.0053 difference (D79)

The same configuration and training seed on seed-21 validation, run in separate processes:

Threads                                Validation C (seed 21, Revision-4b     Epochs                                            Best validation objective
                                       selection, training seed 0)

3                                      0.8246                                 1088                                              2.6340

3                                      0.8337                                 1101                                              2.1799

4                                      0.8284                                 1381                                              2.0173

4                                      0.8284                                 1381                                              2.0173

1                                      0.8222                                 1142                                              2.6181

1                                      0.8222                                 1142                                              2.6181

2                                      0.8207                                 1290                                              2.5957

2                                      0.8207                                 1290                                              2.5957


Explanation.

       Multithreaded floating-point reductions depend on the thread count; at 3 threads they were not even repeatable run to run.
       The training instability then amplified tiny differences into different trajectories.
       Table R4.3 (search, 3 threads) recorded 0.8337. Table R4.5a (diagnostic, 4 threads) recorded 0.8284.

Consequence.

       The Round-4 search compared configurations whose differences (about 0.009) are as large as this numerical spread, so its selection may partly
       reflect noise (disclosed; records unchanged).
       From round 5, all fits are single-threaded.
       After the stability fix, the spread is 0.0006 (R5.3).
R5.2 Revision 4c mechanisms and new tests

         fa_balance: a fixed spectral-path gain, so that the spectral path’s initial RMS on the training data equals the A3 path’s.
         clip: gradient-norm clipping.
         Stopping modes (es_mode):
               two_checkpoint: latent and decoder from the validation-objective minimum; risk from the full-model state at the validation-NLL minimum;
               two_state_refit: after the joint run, the linear AFT head is re-initialised and refitted on the frozen latent with validation-NLL stopping.
         kanfae.evaluation.ceiling: the per-individual parametric plug-in that defines C_ceiling.
         RS-1: with every new option off, the code reproduces the pre-change single-thread fit exactly (validation C 0.8221679197994988, 1142 epochs;
         reports/logs/rs1_regression_check.log).

R5.5 Why Step 2 failed

NLL early stopping ends training at the survival optimum. The diagnostic below refits on the train/validation splits of two confirmation seeds; their test
splits are not touched.

Seed (train/validation         Stop epoch (= min val         Train C                    Val C                            Val oracle C                    Val probe a / b / A / ω
only)                          NLL)

131                            278                           0.8572                     0.8613                           0.9010                          0.886 / 0.727 / 0.841 / 0.864

135                            91                            0.8055                     0.7716                           0.8804                          0.827 / 0.607 / 0.637 / 0.849


Reading.

      On a typical seed (131), training stops around epoch 280 with good concordance, but the b and A probes are still low.
      On seed 135, an early dip in the validation NLL stopped training at epoch 91, before the model had learned much at all.
      The survival optimum and the representation optimum fall at different epochs (D70). The single-state NLL rule resolves the conflict entirely in
      favour of survival.
      The two-state rules keep the representation training. Combined with a burn-in before NLL-based selection, they address both problems. That is the
      recommended next step (§0.3); it needs owner approval and a new pre-registration.


R5.6 Reporting fixes (owner decision 5)

      Chronological test-run tables, in every part: they now include an expected failures (xfail) column and a total column, and every row sums to
      the number of tests in that run. Final suites: 202 in round 3, 209 in round 4.
      Historical parts are rendered from their own snapshots:
            Tests: records up to that round’s final suite run (build_report.use_snapshot).
            Round 1’s C-MAPSS run-status and runtime tables: read round-1-only aggregates (tables/r1_*.csv: no FD003 runs and no v3 re-runs),
            so Option B is no longer double-counted and FD003 no longer appears in round 1.
      The 0.0053 difference is explained in R5.1.

Part S: round-4 report (2026-10-18), historical record
Research prototype report, revision 4 · generated from saved records by scripts/build_report_round4.py · git 69b56f2 (local branch claude/blissful-faraday-2unozw, not
pushed) · status: research prototype, not publication-ready; no successful KAN-FAE model; no novelty claim. Part S is round 4 (owner decisions D67–D69). Parts T–V are the
round-3, round-2 and round-1 reports, kept unchanged as historical records.



R4-0. Round-4 summary (plain English)

R4-0.1 Revision 4b and the revised gate

                                                                                      Result

Design (pre-registered, D71)                                                          Compact frequency-aware front (15 phase-invariant spectral features) + survival-path
                                                                                      regularisation

Selected (validation only, seed 21)                                                   A5-fae_mlp-8e531fd3: head-specific weight decay 1e-2

Revised gate, fresh seed 61                                                           R2: C 0.8372 vs required 0.8662; probe mean 0.755 (ω 0.874)
                                                                             Result

Fresh confirmations, seeds 121–125                                           0/5 pass

Pre-registered verdict                                                       NOT CONFIRMED. KAN vs MLP (H1) and all downstream experiments stay blocked (code
                                                                             guard verified)


R4-0.2 Why it failed, and the most important finding of this round

   1. The overfitting diagnosis was right, but the fixes are not enough.
            With the spectral features, the survival part overfits after about 360 epochs, while the reconstruction part keeps improving until about 2250
            epochs.
            The latent itself generalises.
            Survival-path regularisation selected by the registered rule raised validation C only modestly (0.825 → 0.834).
   2. The latent does not contain enough risk information (D74).
            Replacing the linear head by an MLP head does not help.
            The true risk formula applied to the parameters decodable from the latent does not help either.
   3. The R2 concordance criterion sits at the information limit of the data (D75). This is the key finding.
            Near-optimal estimates of the curve parameters from the raw observations, combined with the true risk formula, fall below oracle − 0.03 on
            9 of 10 never-used seeds.
            The limiting parameter is b, the slope of x₁, which the Gaussian-process noise blurs. Estimating b alone costs about 0.04 in C.
            A learned model that does not know the risk formula cannot be expected to pass R2 reliably, whatever its architecture.
   4. The frequency-aware variants also train unstably: repeated loss spikes, which A3 does not show (D77).

R4-0.3 R1 amendment (owner decision D68): two different procedures, reported side by side

The original R1 (early-stopped σ̂) failed on fresh seeds 601–610 and on gate seed 61. It is not relabelled. The amended R1-A uses the profile σ̂ on
training data with the trained η held fixed, with the same tolerance. R1-A passed on all 10 fresh seeds and on seed 61. The original check measures
optimisation convergence; R1-A measures parameter recovery (R4.4).

R4-0.4 Recommended next scientific step (owner decision required; nothing has been run)

Re-reference R2’s concordance criterion before any further architecture work.

      Why: the current reference, the true-η oracle, is not attainable from these observations.
      How: a prospective, owner-approved amendment would compare C with a data-attainable reference, for example the well-specified parametric
      estimator above evaluated on the same test split (C ≥ C_ref − margin).
      Alternative: keep the oracle reference but change the simulator (less Gaussian-process noise on x₁), which changes the data-generating process.
      Either way, the amended gate must be evaluated on new fresh seeds. The revision-4b results are not re-evaluated post hoc under a new reference.
      Second, independent step: a training-stability study (learning rate, gradient clipping, feature scaling) for the frequency-aware front.

Kind of evidence                                                             Status

Software correctness (tests)                                                 209 tests in the final suite: 203 passed, 2 failed (the current 4b gate’s original R1 and R2:
                                                                             live, real failures), 3 expected failures (historical A3 and revision-4 gates, strict), 1 skipped
                                                                             (documented N/A). The new tests HR-1..HR-3 passed on their first attempt; no test or

Conclusion.

      The oracle in R2 uses the true η. These observations (8–40 noisy samples per curve, with Gaussian-process perturbation of x₁) do not identify the
      slope b well enough to reach oracle − 0.03.
      Even the near-optimal estimator that knows the risk formula falls short on most seeds.
      R2’s concordance criterion, as registered, is not a reachable target for a learned representation of these data. This is not a property
      of KAN or MLP.


R4.6 Recommendation

   1. (Owner decision) Amend R2’s concordance reference prospectively to a data-attainable benchmark computed on the same test split, or
      change the simulator’s noise. Pre-register, and evaluate on new fresh seeds. The old results stay as they are.
   2. (Owner decision) A training-stability study for the frequency-aware front (learning rate, gradient clipping, feature scaling) before any further
      gate look.
   3. Only after the conventional MLP passes an attainable, pre-registered gate: run H1 (matched KAN vs MLP), H2, H3, the controls, and KAN-
      FAE pruning and symbolic extraction, as already specified. The guard remains in place.


R4.7 PBC endpoint (D69): provisional

PBC endpoint: brief scientific justification (for review with the supervising professor)

Status: provisional (owner decisions D58/D69, 2026-10-17/18). Nothing below is a definitive clinical claim. All counts come from
reports/logs/pbc_inspection.json and the saved landmark records (reports/experiment_results.jsonl, phase = descriptive).


1. Data and prediction task

      Source. Mayo Clinic PBC sequential data (pbcseq, R package survival 3.8-12).
            312 patients and 1,945 visits.
            Final status: 143 censored alive, 29 transplanted, 140 died.
      Task (landmark prediction).
            Landmark: s = 730 days.
            Cohort: patients alive and transplant-free at day 730.
            Inputs: the longitudinal markers before the landmark (bilirubin, albumin, alkaline phosphatase, AST, platelets, prothrombin time), plus age
            and sex.
            Target: the residual time from the landmark.
        Landmark cohort. n = 278. The median number of visits before the landmark is 3, and 17% of patients have 2 or fewer.

2. Candidate endpoints

                                           E2 (proposed provisional primary)              E1 (sensitivity)                                 E3 (not implemented)

Event                                      Death or liver transplantation, whichever      Death                                            Death and transplantation as competing
                                           comes first                                                                                     events

Events in the landmark cohort              135 (107 deaths + 28 transplants)              107                                              –

Transplant handling                        Part of the event                              Treated as censoring                             Its own event type

Estimand                                   Distribution of transplant-free survival       Survival in a hypothetical world without         Cause-specific hazards / cumulative
                                           time                                           transplantation                                  incidence of each event

Censoring                                  Alive without transplant at last follow-up     As E2, plus transplantation                      As E2
                                           (administrative / loss to follow-up)

Key assumption                             Censoring non-informative given the            CA-1 must also hold for transplantation,         Correct specification of a competing-risks
                                           landmark covariates (CA-1)                     i.e. transplant unrelated to prognosis given     model
                                                                                          the covariates


3. Why E2 is proposed as the provisional primary endpoint

   1. Transplantation is not a non-informative censoring event. Patients are listed and transplanted because their liver disease is advanced, so
      transplant timing depends on prognosis beyond the measured covariates. Censoring at transplant (E1) then biases survival upward, and its
      estimand describes a hypothetical scenario without transplantation. E2 needs no assumption about transplant selection.
   2. Clinical meaning. Both components mark failure of the native liver, so “transplant-free survival” is a coherent clinical outcome. It is commonly
      used in PBC research. The professor should confirm that this matches the intended clinical question and the conventions of the target literature.
   3. Statistical information. E2 has 135 events against 107 for E1, so estimates and model comparisons are less variable.

4. Limitations of E2 (to discuss)

        Heterogeneous components. E2 combines death and transplantation. Covariate effects can differ between them, and a composite cannot
        separate them.
        Context dependence. Transplantation also depends on factors outside the patient’s biology: organ availability, listing policies, and practice in the
        1974–1984 Mayo era. The composite inherits that dependence.
        Small numbers. With only 28 transplants after the landmark, transplant-specific inference is not feasible in any case.

5. Role of E1 and E3 in the analysis

        E1 is reported as a sensitivity analysis, with its stronger assumption stated explicitly.
        E3 (competing risks) is future work. No competing-risk claims are made. A properly specified cause-specific-hazards or Fine–Gray analysis, with its
        own validation tests, would be needed first.

6. Results so far (descriptive; no model is claimed superior)

        On both endpoints, all validated baselines beat the no-information reference in integrated Brier score (report §R1.10.4).
        KAN-AFT and linear AFT on the same eight landmark inputs could not be told apart over 5 splits (report §R3.5).
        These results do not depend on the endpoint decision being final.

7. Question for the professor

Is transplant-free survival (E2) the appropriate primary estimand for this landmark prediction study, with death-only survival (transplant censored, E1)
as a sensitivity analysis? Should a competing-risks analysis (E3) be planned as a separate, specified study?

What we learned.

   1. The new representation fixed the specific defect it was designed for. The oscillation frequency ω, never decodable before (probe ≈ 0), is
      now decodable on every fresh seed (0.83–0.90). Phase explains only 0.2–1% of the frequency estimate’s error (tests FQ-2, FQ-9).
   2. It created a new problem: overfitting. The spectral block adds 114–408 inputs. Training C rises (0.87–0.91) while validation and test C fall to
      0.80–0.83. A3’s train–validation gap was 0.011; the new front’s is 0.06–0.15.
   3. The diagnostic (validation only) found a partial fix.
            A compact phase-invariant summary (15 features) is the first configuration in the whole project to meet the probe criterion on validation
            (0.82, with ω 0.88).
            Concordance still stays about 0.035 below what R2 requires.
            That variant is a new design (revision 4b). It has not been gate-tested, because it needs your approval and its own pre-registration.
   4. The gate’s own R1 check is not robust.
            R1 uses the true parameters as features. Its σ criterion fails on 8 of 12 seeds (only 4 pass).
            The cause is that σ has not converged when early stopping fires (R3.4).
            The original gate’s R1 pass on seed 21 was a favourable draw.
            No threshold was changed. This needs your decision (R3.9).

R3.1 Motivation and diagnostic (before the design was fixed)

The revision-4 design was motivated by the earlier failures. In rounds 1–2, every front end (A0–A4) failed R2, and ω was never linearly decodable. A
diagnostic on the seed-21 training split only (D60) asked whether ω is recoverable from the curves the models actually see, and with which features.

smoothed_K12                           Quadrature-pair projection            0.824                                0.941                                  0.005
                                       spectrum (new)


Reading.

        ω survives the 12-basis smoothing.
        Fourier power and derivative energy recover ω only partly, because with at most two cycles their values depend on the unknown phase (19–23% of
        the estimate’s error on the smoothed curves).
        The quadrature-pair projection spectrum is essentially phase-free (0.5%).


R3.2 The frequency-aware representation (definition and tests)

The full definition is in docs/design.md §3.2c. In brief, for each smoothed channel x_d(t):
        Projection spectrum. R_d(f) = (‖P_{1,t,sin 2πft,cos 2πft} x_d‖² − ‖P_{1,t} x_d‖²) / ‖x_d − P_{1,t} x_d‖² on 17 or 33 log-spaced frequencies in
        [0.25, 4]. It is exact up to quadrature, computed as fixed quadratic forms cᵀ M_f c of the spline coefficients.
        Log gap. L = −log(1 − R + 10⁻⁴), which separates the exact peak R = 1 from the low-frequency plateau that a ≤ 2-cycle window produces.
        Derivative energies. log ∫(x − trend)², log ∫x′², log ∫x″².
        Soft frequency. f̂_d = Σ_j f_j softmax(κ_d L_d(f_j)).

These are standardised with training statistics, mapped linearly and added to the A3 front. With the spectral weights at zero, the front equals A3 exactly
(FQ-6).

Reading.

      The C criterion passes on every seed.
      The σ criterion fails on most seeds, and σ̂ falls as the stopping epoch rises.
      The profile MLE of σ, with the learned η held fixed, separates two explanations:
             non-convergence at the early-stopping epoch;
             a genuine misfit.
      The σ̂ at early stopping correlates −0.91 with the stopping epoch, while the profile σ̂ lies within ±0.05 of the truth on 12 of 12 seeds (mean
      0.487).
      The likelihood and the oracle head are sound. The registered σ check fails because σ, initialised at 0.69, has not converged when
      early stopping on the validation NLL fires. The R1 threshold was not changed.


R3.5 PBC: E2 provisional primary endpoint, E1 sensitivity (D58)

E2: death or transplantation (transplant-free survival). Provisional primary endpoint.

      Interpretation: time until the native liver fails (death or need for transplantation).
      Censoring: alive without transplant at last follow-up, assumed non-informative given the landmark covariates (CA-1).
      Transplantation is part of the event, so no assumption about transplant selection is needed.
      Not claimed as a definitive clinical endpoint until confirmed with the owner’s professor.

R3.6 C-MAPSS: Option B primary RUL benchmark, Option A secondary (D59, D62)

Option B (trailing 30-cycle windows every 10 cycles; landmark s as a covariate). Primary.

        Evaluation: the internal test engines, plus the official test set (last window per engine).
        Within-engine correlation: windows from the same engine are correlated, so uncertainty comes from an engine-cluster bootstrap (test engines
        resampled with replacement, 1000 resamples), and the engine-weighted RMSE gives each engine equal weight.
        Framing: C-MAPSS has no genuine right censoring. These are RUL-benchmark metrics, separate from the right-censored evaluation on PBC.

R2-0. Final summary (plain English)

R2-0.1 Learnability gate: the result you asked to see

The gate checks, on simulated data with a known answer, whether the conventional functional autoencoder (MLP version) learns the risk-relevant
information well enough for a KAN-versus-MLP comparison to mean anything. Requirement R2:

        test C-index ≥ oracle − 0.03;
        the latent code must linearly reveal the four hidden curve parameters (a, b, A, ω), with mean probe R² ≥ 0.8.
                                                                                              Result

Configuration selected by the controlled search (validation data only)                        A3-fae_mlp-ab243462: tensor-spline functional front end, latent size 8, α = 1, Adam 3e-3

Official gate (seed 21), final run                                                            R1 PASS (C 0.8910); R2 FAIL: C 0.8497 vs required 0.8636; probe a / b / A / ω = 0.928 /
                                                                                              0.864 / 0.848 / 0.014, mean 0.663 vs 0.8; R3 PASS (|ΔC| 0.0068)

Fresh replications, D41 (seeds 101–105)                                                       0/5 pass (C − threshold from -0.0213 to -0.0067)

Fresh replications, D46 (seeds 106–110)                                                       0/5 pass (C − threshold from -0.0237 to -0.0072)

Pre-registered verdict (D46)                                                                  R2 FAILED. Not confirmed. No further extension.


What this means. Across the design iterations the gap to the required C-index shrank from −0.109 (first attempt) to −0.014 (final gate run), and three
of the four hidden parameters became well decoded (gate probe R² 0.85–0.93). The fourth, the oscillation frequency ω, stayed poorly decoded: probe R²
≤ 0.2 in every configuration and ≈ 0 for the selected one. The exception was the derivative-energy front end (validation ω probe 0.43), and that front end
lost more elsewhere than it gained. Under the rules fixed before the search, the KAN-versus-MLP comparison (H1) and everything that depends on it
remain blocked. We therefore have no evidence for or against KAN in the functional autoencoder.

R2-0.2 What we achieved in this round

   1. Reference-based audit. Every equation is mapped to its file, function and test (I.2). The audit found 3 missing features (KAN regularisation,
      pruning, symbolic extraction), 1 mathematical limitation in a reference estimator (the transform estimator is biased on the log scale), and, during
      the round, 1 real code defect (a feature-cache defect; fixed, regression-tested, all affected results recomputed). It also found 1 process gap: unit
      tests were not re-run after the D45 change of defaults, so two tests went stale (fixed in D56; the final full-suite run is clean apart from R2).
   2. Survival losses. Buckley–James, IPCW and transform least squares were implemented as separate validated variants. Their behaviour under
      different censoring assumptions was measured (I.4). The Cox partial likelihood was not inserted into the AFT model.
   3. Systematic recovery of the R2 failure. A pre-registered, validation-only controlled search (17 fits) varied the front end, latent size, loss weight,
      optimiser, early stopping, encoder, training budget, derivative energy and capacity. It was followed by independent confirmations on 10 fresh data
      seeds (I.1). Outcome: an honest FAIL.
   4. KAN regularisation, pruning and mandatory symbolic extraction (linear → library → PySR, accepted only at validation R² > 0.99), validated
      on known truth with KAN-AFT. The true shapes (tanh, quadratic, sine) were recovered under the parametric, Buckley–James and IPCW losses. 34/47
      edge formulas were accepted overall. Substituting the formulas changed test C by at most 0.002 (I.5, I.6).
   5. Real-data KAN-AFT on PBC with formulas (41/80 accepted), against a linear AFT on the same inputs: no consistent difference (I.7).
   6. Ledger items closed:
             interval likelihood (L14);
             censoring-assumption and misspecification study (L16);
             C-MAPSS FD003 baselines (L15, partial);
             targeted literature review (L17).

R2.1.2 Controlled search (validation data only; D41 steps S1–S7, D46 steps S8–S10)

      Selection rule (fixed in D41 before any fit). Maximise validation C among configurations whose mean validation probe R² ≥ 0.8; if none
      qualifies, maximise validation C + 0.1 × probe mean. Ties keep the simpler configuration. (Wording corrected 2026-10-18, D73: an earlier version of
      this sentence said “passing both validation criteria”, which misdescribed the registered rule; the code always implemented the registered rule.)
      Search order. Greedy, one factor at a time:
             S1 front end: A0 linear (Wu et al.), A1 pointwise-MLP NFL, A2 energy ∫γx², A3 tensor spline ∫F(x(t), t)dt;
             S2 latent size;
             S3 α;
             S4 optimiser (Adam / AdamW / learning rate);
             S5 early-stopping target;
             S6 encoder (linear / MLP / KAN; information only);
             S7 seeds;
             S8 epoch budget;
             S9 derivative-energy front A4;
             S10 capacity.
      What the search never used: the test split, the gate seed’s test data and the replication seeds.
