Seed 110 and the cache defect.

        Original result. Before the fix, seed 110 gave test C 0.4913 (chance level), although its train and validation C were 0.856 and 0.838. That pattern
        was impossible for a sound model, so it was investigated rather than reported as a model failure.
        Root cause (D53).
              TensorSplineFunctional.features cached features under the key (memory address, shape, version) without keeping the input alive.
              The validation and test splits have the same size, so the test tensor could reuse the freed validation tensor’s address and receive the
              validation features.
        Fix. The cache now keeps the input tensor and matches only the same object.
        Regression test F8b fails on the old code (74% of elements wrong) and passes on the fix.
        Recomputed seed 110. Test C 0.8413 (threshold 0.8561): still a FAIL, but now a legitimate one.
        Everything else affected was recomputed:
              the search: same validation values, same selection;
              the gate: identical result;
              seeds 101–109: identical.
        Records. The superseded records are kept in reports/superseded_D53/.

R2.1.4 Interpretation

        The failure is specific and repeatable. Every selected-configuration fit decodes a, b and the amplitude A reasonably well (probe R² 0.68–0.94;
        mostly above 0.8), but not the frequency ω (|probe R²| ≤ 0.083), and C falls short of the threshold in all 11 evaluations (gate plus 10 replications)
        by 0.007–0.024.
        The design reason (audit A-PROBE). ω enters the risk through the oscillation’s derivative energy, and a latent of size 8 that also has to
        reconstruct the curves does not linearly expose ω.
        The direct fix did not pay off. The derivative-energy front A4 raised the ω probe (validation 0.43) but lowered the others and C.
        Conclusion: no legitimate configuration in the registered search space passed R2. Changing the threshold, the probe definition or the
        data would invalidate the gate (D11, D39), so this is reported as a failure.

Consequence for claims

       Functional autoencoders (Wu et al.), KAN survival models (CoxKAN, KAN-AFT, SurvKAN, KAPLAN-HR), autoencoder-survival models (AESurv, SAVAE)
       and KAN-based functional learning with reconstruction (FunKAN) all exist.
       Combining a functional KAN autoencoder with a censoring-aware AFT likelihood was not found as a single published method in this targeted search.
       However, the components are all established, and FunKAN’s full text could not be checked.
       No novelty claim is made. A claim would need a systematic review (databases, search strings, screening log), which this is not.

Known reference discrepancies (recorded, not resolved)

       KAN-AFT cites “Fan & Gijbels [8]” for the transformation estimator. Its reference [8] is Fan, Gijbels & King (1997), Local likelihood and local partial
       likelihood in hazard regression, which does not appear to be the synthetic-data transformation source.
       KAN-AFT states CA-1 (C ⊥ T | z) but uses a marginal Kaplan–Meier estimate of censoring in IPCW and the transform. That is consistent only under
       CA-2.
       KAN-AFT’s Buckley–James imputes on the time scale and then takes logs, unlike the classical log-scale imputation.
       The CoxKAN 22-function symbolic library is defined only in its supplementary material, which was not obtained. Our library is therefore our own
       documented list (src/kanfae/symbolic/fit.py).

R2.4 Survival losses: parametric likelihood vs censoring-adjusted least squares

      Estimator validation (all passed; details in I.11).
           LS-1: no censoring reduces every estimator to OLS.
           LS-2: the KM and Buckley–James conditional means match a brute-force reference.
           LS-3: the transform integral and non-negativity.
           LS-4: slope recovery.
           LS-5: unbiasedness of T* on the time scale.

Censoring-assumption and misspecification study (L16, D50).

      Model: log T = 1 + 0.8x₁ − 0.5x₂ + ε; n = 2000; 20 replicates per scenario.
      Scenarios:
           CA2: censoring independent of everything;
           CA1: censoring depends on x₁ (still independent of T given x);
           MIS: skewed mixture errors.
      Reading the results:
           Only the parametric log-normal likelihood (correct family) and Buckley–James are close to unbiased in all three scenarios.
           Marginal-KM IPCW is biased once censoring depends on covariates, as theory predicts (it needs CA-2).
           The transform estimator is biased on the log scale in every scenario (A-TRANSFORM).
           The Weibull likelihood is mildly biased, being the wrong family here.
           IPCW with the true conditional censoring distribution, an oracle reference only, still shows bias under CA1, because some subjects have
           censoring weights that are very large (practical positivity).

Consequence for KAN-FAE. The parametric likelihood stays the loss for the functional autoencoders:

       it is the only one that is a fixed, differentiable per-individual loss that can be summed with the reconstruction loss;
       it is valid under CA-1;
       it gives survival curves directly.

Buckley–James is the robust alternative when the error family is in doubt, but it needs an outer impute-and-refit loop.


R2.5 KAN regularisation and pruning (before/after)

       Regularisation: λ(|Φ|₁ + λ_ent S(Φ) + λ_coef |C|₁), as in CoxKAN Eqs. 5–8 and KAN-AFT L_R, with λ chosen on validation data from {0, 1e-3, 1e-2}.
       Pruning: edge L1 < θ = 1e-2, plus node pruning min(I, O) < θ for deeper KANs (KAN-AFT).
       Before/after metrics are in the table above (spline → pruned → formulas) and in I.7 for PBC.
       Only 1 of 22 fits pruned an edge (synthetic seed 203, IPCW, λ = 1e-2: it removed exactly the true null edge z₄). In the other 21, “pruned” equals
       “unpruned”.

The diagnostic below (D54, registered before running; not used for selection) explains why:

       the reference score mean |φ| includes each edge’s constant offset, which is not identifiable in an additive model, so the null edge can score higher
       than a true edge;
       the offset-free (centred) score separates the null edge cleanly, but its value (~0.03) is above θ = 1e-2 unless λ ≥ 0.1, which validation did not
       select.

θ was not changed.

R2.6 Symbolic formula extraction

       Procedure (mandatory, staged).
              Stage 1: linear a·x + b.
              Stage 2: a library of 15 functions in the affine form c·f(a·x + b) + d, fitted by grid search plus Levenberg–Marquardt, each with a domain
              check.
              Stage 3: PySR 2.7.0.
       Acceptance. A formula is accepted only if its R² on held-out points (30% of the edge’s training inputs, never used for fitting) exceeds 0.99,
       following CoxKAN.
       Rejection. A rejected edge keeps its learned spline, so nothing is fabricated.
       Effect of substitution. This is evaluated separately (test C, IBS and curve error in the I.4 table).
       Inputs. x is the standardised covariate.
       Truth R² compares the learned edge with the true component on z ∈ [−2, 2] (synthetic only).

PBC (real data): accepted formulas and their stability across the 5 splits.

       An accepted formula means that the fitted spline is well described by that formula on that split.
       The family chosen for the same covariate changes between splits.
       So the formulas describe shapes and are not stable laws. The full per-split table is in Appendix A.

R2.9 Interval (integer-cycle) likelihood (L14)

aft_interval_log_likelihood gives:

         events: log[S(y − 1) − S(y)];
         censored observations: log S(y);

computed in a stable log-difference form.

Tests:

         INT-1 compares it with a 200-digit mpmath reference. It failed once because the original float64 scipy reference lost up to 7 digits to cancellation;
         that was a defect in the test reference, not in the code (D48). The tolerance was kept.
         INT-2 checks that a narrow interval approaches the density.
         INT-3 checks gradients and extreme values.

The likelihood is implemented and tested, but not yet used in an experiment.

D38               Design revision: nonlinear          APPROVED by owner 2026-10-17;        The first layer of the functional         The gate diagnosis showed that
                  functional features (owner chose    specification fixed before any run   autoencoders becomes a nonlinear          linear functionals cannot express
                  D33 option (a))                                                          functional layer (NFL): h_j = b_j         phase-invariant amplitude features
                                                                                           + Σ_d Σ_m ∫ β_jdm(t)
                                                                                           g_dm(x_d(t)) dt, with g_d(x) =
                                                                                           [x, MLP_d(x)]. Each MLP_d is a per-
                                                                                           channel pointwise network 1 → 16 →
                                                                                           4 (SiLU), shared over time. So M = 5
                                                                                           feature maps per channel, including
                                                                                           the identity, and each β_jdm is a
                                                                                           cubic B-spline with K_β = 8 and the
                                                                                           same roughness penalty. The integral
                                                                                           is evaluated by Gauss–Legendre
                                                                                           quadrature, 8 nodes per sub-interval
                                                                                           of the union of both bases’ break
                                                                                           points, on the smoothed curve
                                                                                           x_d(t) = Σ_k c_dk φ_k(t). This is
                                                                                           the deferred ∫F(x(t),t)dt family
                                                                                           (D2-R), with F(x,t) = Σ_m β_m(t)
                                                                                           g_m(x). The NFL is shared by both
                                                                                           comparison arms: MLP and KAN still
                                                                                           differ only in the encoder/decoder
                                                                                           blocks, whose parameter matching
                                                                                           (D31) is unchanged. All other settings
                                                                                           are unchanged (H = 32, MLP hidden
                                                                                           64, r = 4, 3000 epochs, patience 100,
                                                                                           α = 1, S2). The original linear first
                                                                                           layer stays available as
                                                                                           front="linear" for reproducing
                                                                                           earlier results.

D39               Integrity safeguards for the gate   ADOPTED before any run               (1) The gate criteria R1–R3, their        Research integrity (D0, D11)
                  re-run                                                                   thresholds and seed 21 are
                                                                                           unchanged. (2) The revision was
                                                                                           motivated by diagnostics on the gate
                                                                                           data, which risks tailoring the design
                                                                                           to the gate. To limit this, the
                                                                                           pointwise nonlinearity is a generic
                                                                                           learned function (not a hand-picked
                                                                                           x² or amplitude feature), and its
                                                                                           hyperparameters (M = 5, width 16,
                                                                                           quadrature) are fixed in this entry
                                                                                           before any run. (3) A pass is therefore
                                                                                           weaker evidence than a first-attempt
                                                                                           pass, and it will be reported as such.
                                                                                           The H1 replicates (seeds 1000–1004)
                                                                                           are independent of the gate data. (4)
                                                                                           This is a fresh attempt series for the
                                                                                           revised design under the standard
                                                                                           failure policy: at most 2 targeted

                                                                                           the gate re-run. H1–H3 and the

D42   Censoring-adjusted least-squares       ADOPTED as separate model   Implemented as separate estimators        Owner request; mathematical
      estimators (BJ, IPCW, transform),      variants                    of the AFT location function η(z). The    differences documented
      from KAN-AFT Appendix A                                            parametric likelihood remains the
                                                                         reference for the functional
                                                                         autoencoders. Differences recorded:
                                                                         (1) BJ: the classical log-scale
                                                                         imputation E[ε | ε > e_i] (Buckley
                                                                         & James 1979) is primary; KAN-AFT’s
                                                                         time-scale variant log E[r | r >
                                                                         r_i] is available as an option and
                                                                         differs by Jensen’s inequality. (2)
                                                                         IPCW: w_i = δ_i / Ĝ(T̃_i−), with Ĝ
                                                                         the marginal Kaplan–Meier estimate
                                                                         of censoring. This requires CA-2
                                                                         (censoring independent of covariates)
                                                                         and positivity, which is stronger than
                                                                         the CA-1 stated in KAN-AFT. (3)
                                                                         Transform: T* = φ₁(T̃)δ + φ₂(T̃)
                                                                         (1−δ) is unbiased for E[T|z] on the
                                                                         time scale; regressing log T* is not
                                                                         unbiased for E[log T|z] (Jensen). This
                                                                         is reported, not corrected. (4) None of
                                                                         the three estimates σ or the error
                                                                         law; survival curves are obtained
                                                                         from the Kaplan–Meier estimate of
                                                                         censored residuals (homoscedastic
                                                                         semiparametric AFT).

Project instructions (the repository README.md is intentionally left unchanged, D28).

R2.15 Limitations and decisions requested from the owner

        R2 failed under the pre-registered protocol (D46: no further extension), so KAN-FAE is not ready for H1. Legitimate next steps need
        your decision, because each changes the scientific question:
              (a) Change the simulator’s risk so that it does not hinge on a frequency that a reconstruction-driven latent cannot expose linearly. This
              changes the gate’s question and needs a new pre-registration.
              (b) Give the probe criterion a nonlinear decoder. This changes R2’s definition; it is not done here, because D11 forbids relaxing it
              automatically.
              (c) Adopt a front end with explicit spectral features, such as a learned Fourier/derivative energy at several scales, as a new design revision
              with a fresh gate.
              (d) Proceed to H1 with the failure disclosed. This is not recommended: a KAN-vs-MLP comparison is uninformative when both arms fail to
              learn the signal.
        PBC endpoint (E1 vs E2 vs competing risks) and C-MAPSS landmark design (A vs B) are still your decisions.
        Reference copies. The uploaded reference PDFs were not available in the session, so the public arXiv versions were used. They may differ from
        the uploaded copies.
        Pruning. The pruning threshold θ = 1e-2 from the references did not remove a true null covariate at the validation-selected λ (D54). A centred
        score would, but it is not adopted without your decision.
        Formula stability. Real-data formulas are shape descriptions, not stable laws (I.6).
        Statistical power. With 5 splits on PBC, small differences cannot be detected.

Research prototype report · generated 2026-10-16 from saved results by scripts/build_report.py · git 69b56f2 (local branch claude/blissful-faraday-2unozw, not pushed) ·
status: research prototype, not publication-ready · no novelty claim is made.



R1.1 Executive summary (plain English)

What we set out to test. Whether a new kind of neural network building block, the Kolmogorov–Arnold network (KAN), helps a “functional autoencoder”
predict time-to-event from patient-like or machine-like measurements that change over time, compared with a matched conventional network (an MLP).

What we did.

       Built the prototype in small validated stages:
              a survival-likelihood module that correctly handles incomplete (censored) follow-up;
              a simulator with a known answer;
              the functional representation and our own KAN layer;
              the models;
              evaluation metrics.
       Checked each stage against independent reference calculations before moving on.

The most important result.

       Before comparing KAN with MLP, we required the conventional functional autoencoder to pass a pre-agreed learnability check: on simulated data
       with a known answer, it had to get close to the best achievable accuracy. It did not.
              Required: a concordance (C-index) of at least 0.8636.
              Achieved: 0.8361, even after the two permitted repairs (longer training, more capacity).
       The likely reason is that the risk depended on the size of an oscillation, and the model’s first layer can only take weighted averages of the curves,
       which cannot directly measure size when the oscillation’s timing varies.
       Under the rule we fixed in advance, this blocked the KAN-vs-MLP comparison.


  So this prototype provides no evidence that KAN helps, and no evidence that it does not. The key comparison was correctly not run.


What did run.

       Validated, conventional baselines on:
             simulated data;
             NASA C-MAPSS turbofan data (real benchmark data with no genuinely incomplete follow-up; mainly a remaining-useful-life benchmark);
             PBC liver-disease data (real data with genuinely incomplete follow-up).
       On simulated data, simple per-channel summaries (last value, mean, spread, trend) beat the “weighted-average” FPCA approach. This is consistent
       with the learnability finding.
       On PBC, all baselines clearly beat a no-information reference, but they could not be told apart reliably. The PBC patients had only about 3
       measurements each before the prediction time, too few for functional modelling to be reliable.

What is still open (your decisions).

       How to revise the architecture so that it can pass the gate.
       Which PBC endpoint to adopt.
       Which C-MAPSS landmark design to adopt.

Test status. 150 test cases; latest outcomes: 148 passed, 1 failed (the learnability check R2), 1 skipped (documented not-applicable case). Every
attempt, including failures, is logged.


R1.2 Research objective and hypotheses

Narrow research question. Does a KAN-based functional representation improve survival prediction from multivariate time-varying trajectories over
parameter-matched conventional baselines?

Hypotheses were fixed in docs/design.md §8.3 and docs/experiment_protocol.md §6 before any experiment ran (decision D24):

R1.5 Model architecture, equations and key design choices

The full specification is in docs/design.md.

R1.5.1 Landmark prediction

A trajectory observed on a window ending at landmark s is used to predict the residual time T* − s for individuals at risk at s. No input is dated after s
(test K4).
R1.5.2 Censoring-aware AFT likelihood

 log T = η + σ ε,     w = (log y − η)/σ,      S(t) = S_ε((log t − η)/σ)
 ℓ_i = δ_i [log f_ε(w_i) − log σ − log y_i] + (1 − δ_i) log S_ε(w_i)
 Weibull: log f = w − e^w,          log S = −e^w
 Log-normal: log f = −w²/2 − ½ log 2π,   log S = log Φ(−w)
 Log-logistic: log f = w − 2 softplus(w), log S = −softplus(w)



R1.5.3 Functional representation

       Smoother: a quadrature-weighted penalised B-spline smoother (D20): c = (ΦᵀQΦ + λR + λ₀I)⁻¹ ΦᵀQy, with cell-length weights Q. The data term
       therefore approximates ∫ (y − x)² dt and is consistent under refinement of the sampling (test F3).
       Functional linear layer: h_j = b_j + Σ_d ∫ β_jd(t) x_d(t) dt = b_j + Σ_d c_dᵀ J b_jd.

R1.5.4 Autoencoders

       Encoder and decoder: z = g_enc(h); ĉ = g_dec(z); x̂(t) = Σ_k ĉ_k φ_k(t); head η = wᵀ[z, u] + b.
       Reconstruction loss: weights every individual equally (D19).
       Total loss: L = mean(−ℓ) + α·L_rec + λ_β Σ bᵀR_βb.

R1.5.5 KAN layer and parameter matching

       KAN layer (in-house; passed F-KAN-1..4): out_q = Σ_p [w^b_pq SiLU(x_p) + w^s_pq Σ_g a_pqg B_g(x_p)] + bias_q. Cubic B-splines on a uniform grid of 5
       intervals on [−2, 2], preceded by a per-feature BatchNorm (D30).
       Parameter matching (D31): KAN encoder and decoder blocks are chosen automatically to be within ±10% of the MLP blocks, avoiding
       bottlenecks narrower than r.
             Original defaults: 2120 vs 2024 parameters (+4.7%).
             Repaired defaults: 5090 vs 5032 (+1.2%).
             For D ≥ 6, a decoder hidden width of 3 < r is unavoidable under matching; this is a recorded limitation.

R1.5.6 Key corrections made before any training

       D30: BatchNorm instead of LayerNorm. A per-sample LayerNorm would have removed 2 of the 4 latent degrees of freedom.
       D31: the matching rule.
       D32: M2 targets that each model can represent.
       D36 (later): linear-AFT penalty scaling, found during the C-MAPSS smoke test.

Synthetic data.

       Observed and oracle objects are separate (tests G5, G6, M5).
       Censoring is independent of everything, so marginal-KM IPCW is appropriate by construction (D17).
       15% of each test individual’s points (for individuals with ≥ 4 points) are held out for reconstruction metrics.

C-MAPSS.

       Inspected before any loader was written (reports/logs/cmapss_inspection.json). There are no missing values and cycles are consecutive.
       Note: the dataset readme lists the columns up to “sensor measurement 26”, but there are 26 columns and 21 sensors.
       Sensors are selected on training engines only (standard deviation ≥ 1e-6).
       Option A uses the full history [1, s0] with s0 = minimum training-split life − 1.
       Option B uses trailing 30-cycle windows every 10 cycles, with s/100 as a covariate. Engine-level splits (K3) and no input after the landmark (K4) are
       tested.

PBC.

       Help page vs data:
             the follow-up column is futime (the help page says time);
             trig and copper are listed but absent;
             chol is 42% missing and was excluded (D26);
             missing visit rows: alk.phos 3.1%, platelet 3.8%.
       Channels: log(bili), albumin, log(alk.phos), log(ast), platelet, log(protime). Missing values are masked (never imputed into the loss).
       The help page documents that extra visits were often prompted by worsening condition.

Explanations (each failure got at most two targeted repairs; no threshold was changed, D11).

       Stage A, A2 (all three families), attempts 1–2: test-harness bugs.
            Quadrature over (−∞, ∞) overflowed exp(u) and gave NaN.
            A wide finite range then missed the narrow density peak at σ = 0.2.
            Repair 2 integrates on the standardised scale w.
            The likelihood code itself was never changed.
       Stage A, A7 (log-logistic, then log-normal): the reference optimiser.
            Our maximised log-likelihood was 7.8e-4 higher than lifelines’.
            lifelines’ SLSQP stopped early.
            A diagnostic showed our likelihood evaluated at lifelines’ own estimates equals lifelines’ value within 1e-8.
            Tightening lifelines’ ftol resolved it.
       Stage E, Q1, attempts 1–2: fixture issues.
            The scikit-survival reference cannot evaluate the training censoring KM beyond the largest training time.
            Our IBS now evaluates G at min(Y_i, t_last), which is exact.
            The fixture uses test times inside the support.
       Stage D, learnability gate: R2 FAILED after both permitted repairs (§10.1).


R1.9 Baselines, splits, seeds, tuning rules and metrics

Models actually run (validated, non-neural).

Model                                                Representation                                                  Head

FPCA + AFT                                           FPCA scores                                                     Linear Weibull AFT

FPCA + Cox                                           FPCA scores (secondary reference)                               Cox

Summary + AFT                                        Last value, mean, sd, OLS slope per channel, plus u             Penalised linear Weibull AFT

Summary + Cox                                        Same summary features                                           Penalised Cox

Summary + RSF                                        Same summary features                                           Random survival forest, 200 trees


       References (not comparators, no tuning): a covariate-free Kaplan–Meier prediction (km_null, D35) and, on synthetic data only, the true model
       (oracle_true).
       Not run (BLOCKED, D33): functional MLP autoencoder, KAN functional autoencoder, flattened autoencoder, and all ablations AB1–AB8.

Splits.

       Synthetic: 5 independent replicate data sets (seeds 1000–1004), each split 60/20/20, stratified on δ.
       C-MAPSS: 5 engine-level splits (seeds 0–4). Official test engines are evaluated separately.
       PBC: 5 patient-level splits, stratified on δ.

Leakage controls. Fitted on training data only (test K2):

       channel standardisation;
       smoother λ;
       FPCA;
       sensor selection;
       summary-feature scaling;
       the censoring models;
       all hyperparameters.
Tuning (D22).

       Each model gets 4 configurations at seed 0, selected by validation IBS.
       Grids:
              FPCA: r ∈ {2, 4, 8, 12}
              Summary AFT: L2 ∈ {1e-3, 1e-2, 0.1, 1} (per observation)
              Summary Cox: penaliser ∈ {0.01, 0.1, 1, 10}
              RSF: min_samples_leaf ∈ {5, 10, 20, 40}
       The selected RSF configuration is re-run with seeds 1 and 2 and averaged within the replicate. Deterministic models run once.

Metrics (protocol §5, D6).

       Synthetic primary: survival-curve error, mean_i (1/t_max) ∫₀^{t_max} |Ŝ_i − S_i| dt.
       Real data primary: IBS with marginal-KM IPCW. For PBC this is flagged as a limitation (D17), with a conditional (Cox censoring model) IPCW
       sensitivity analysis.
       Secondary: Uno’s C (truncated at the 90th percentile of test times); Harrell’s C; D-calibration (10 bins); calibration-in-the-large at the 25th, 50th
       and 75th percentile horizons.
       C-MAPSS RUL: RMSE and MAE of the median predicted residual life (uncapped), reported separately from survival metrics.

Uncertainty. Mean ± SD over replicates or splits. The pre-registered paired test was planned for H1 only, and H1 was not run. Comparisons between
baselines are descriptive.

R1.10 Experimental results

All results below are actual outputs of logged runs (reports/experiment_results.jsonl and .csv; summaries in reports/tables/). Values are mean ± SD
over 5 replicates or splits. For the random survival forest, values are first averaged over seeds 0–2 within each replicate. n is the number of
replicates/splits contributing.


  Data labels. §10.2 is SYNTHETIC. §10.3 is REAL (C-MAPSS, simulated turbofan; RUL benchmark, no natural censoring); its survival-
  framing metrics involve no censoring, except in §10.3.3, which is ARTIFICIAL CENSORING. §10.4 is REAL (PBC, genuinely right-censored).



R1.10.1 Learnability gate (SYNTHETIC; seed 21; N = 2000; stage D)

      R1 PASS. An MLP AFT head given the true latent parameters (a, b, A, ω) reached test C = 0.8910 (oracle 0.8936), with σ = 0.4816 (truth 0.5). The
      survival head and likelihood can learn the known nonlinear relationship when the right features are available.

      R2 FAIL (pre-specified: C ≥ oracle − 0.03 = 0.8636, and mean probe R² ≥ 0.8). For the functional MLP autoencoder:

        Attempt                         Change                            Test C                          Probe R² (a, b, A, ω)              Mean probe R²

        1                               As specified                      0.7545                          0.861 0.711 0. 0.022               0.398

        2                               Repair 1: training budget 400 →   0.8050                          0.8 0.525 0.257 0.035              0.404
                                        3000 epochs (the cap was always
                                        hit)

        3                               Repair 2: capacity, H 16 → 32,    0.8361                          0.799 0.468 0.449 0.166            0.471
                                        hidden 32 → 64


      R3 PASS at attempt 3.

              |C − C_R2| = 0.0042.
              The censoring-aware model had a smaller survival-curve error than the naive model (censored times treated as events) at all 3 seeds: aware
              0.0958, 0.0976, 0.0998 vs naive 0.1472, 0.1451, 0.1487.
              At attempts 1 and 2, the |C − C_R2| part failed (0.0313, 0.0247) while the censoring part already passed.




      Learnability gate

Diagnosis (interpretation, labelled as such).

      The largest risk term is −0.8·A², where A is the amplitude of a sinusoid with a random phase. That is a phase-invariant (quadratic) functional of the
      trajectory.
      The architecture’s first layer computes only linear functionals ∫β(t) x(t) dt. The downstream network must learn the energy-like combination, and
      at N = 1200 training individuals it under-fits: train C ≈ test C ≈ 0.79–0.84 in reports/logs/diag_R2_capacity.log. Capacity beyond H = 32 did not help
      (plateau ≈ 0.836).
      Consequence (pre-registered rule, D33): the KAN-vs-MLP primary comparison (H1), H2, H3 and all ablations were not run.
      Diagnostic observation only, not evidence for H1: in one gate-data run at a single seed with a 3000-epoch budget, the KAN autoencoder
      reached C = 0.837 vs 0.805 for the MLP at its original size (reports/logs/diag_R2_budget.log). This single-seed observation on the gate data set must
      not be read as a KAN advantage.

R1.10.3.3 Option A with ARTIFICIAL CENSORING (code-path test only)

Training and validation targets were censored independently with C ~ U(0, max training residual). Test targets are uncensored. These numbers test the
censoring code path, not real censoring.

Observations (descriptive; no significance claims).

      Option A, internal test. RUL RMSE was 18.4 (FPCA + AFT), 17.9 (FPCA + Cox) and 18.2 (Summary + Cox) cycles, against 47.5 for the null
      reference.
      Option A, official test. Only engines whose observed length reaches s0 can be evaluated (mean 54.8 of 100). FPCA + AFT had the lowest RMSE,
      23.0.
      Option B, official test (all 100 engines at their last cycle). Summary + RSF had the lowest RMSE, 18.9. The parametric/Cox baselines were at
      27.2–29.4, and the null reference at 44.2.
      Option B, internal test pooled over all landmarks. RMSE was ≈34.2–37.2. Per band it falls from ≈47.0 at early landmarks (30–99) to ≈10.8 at
      late landmarks (≥ 200). Discrimination within the early band is modest (C ≈ 0.671), as expected when degradation is not yet visible.
      The two options are not directly comparable. They predict at different landmarks and evaluate different official-test subsets. This is one
      reason D3b remains an owner decision.
      Artificial censoring (Option A).
             The parametric AFT predictions stayed close to their uncensored values: FPCA + AFT internal RMSE 20.7 vs 18.4.
           For the Cox models, some predicted survival curves never fell to 0.5 within the training follow-up, so their medians are undefined. On average
           1.0 test engines per split were affected for Summary + Cox; these are flagged in the records and set to the grid end. This inflates Cox RMSE
           (38.6 ± 41.2).
           For Summary + AFT, all four configurations diverged in one split, so only 4 of 5 splits contribute.
      The neural autoencoders were not evaluated (BLOCKED, D33).

R1.10.4.3 Visit process (descriptive; full cohort; not used as a model feature)

Endpoint              Cohort                Events                Visits ≤ 730 d:       ≤ 2 visits            HR per visit (95% CI)   p
                                                                  median (range)

pbc_E1                278                   107                   3 (1–5)               17%                   0.897 (0.695–1.158)     0.403

pbc_E2                278                   135                   3 (1–5)               17%                   0.983 (0.780–1.239)     0.885


Observations (descriptive; no significance claims).

      All baselines improved substantially on the covariate-free reference for both endpoints.
              E1: IBS 0.116–0.129 vs 0.204 for the null.
              E2: IBS 0.133–0.140 vs 0.222.
      Differences between baselines were small relative to their split-to-split SDs, so no ranking is claimed. With about 56 test patients per
      split, the uncertainty is large.
      The conditional-IPCW sensitivity analysis changed IBS values by less than about 0.01.
              E1: FPCA + Cox 0.116 (marginal) vs 0.114 (conditional).
              E2: 0.135 vs 0.141.
              So, under the Cox censoring model used, the metric conclusions are not sensitive to the CA-2 assumption. This does not validate CA-1 for
              transplant under E1.
      D-calibration p-values were all > 0.05. With small test sets this test has little power.
      FPCA-based and summary-feature baselines performed similarly. This is unsurprising given a median of 3 visits per patient (§14). The data
      are too sparse to make the functional representation informative.
      Visit process (descriptive). The univariate hazard ratio per additional visit in the window is reported in the table above. The absence of a clear
      association in this crude check does not rule out an informative visit process; the dataset documentation itself describes visits triggered by
      worsening condition.

R1.13 What was learned

   1. The censoring-aware AFT machinery is validated. All three AFT likelihoods matched independent references:
            scipy closed forms (rtol = 1e-10);
            numerical integration and autograd hazards (1e-8);
            lifelines maximum likelihood (1e-4);
            recovery of the truth within 3 SE at a fixed seed.
      The synthetic generator passed all 12 generator criteria, including oracle isolation and invariance of the loss to hidden event times.
   2. The functional representation is numerically sound. Discretisation consistency held at roughly O(1/n²) (F3), and the in-house KAN layer
      passed its own tests.
   3. The proposed functional autoencoder failed its learnability gate (R2). Under controlled conditions it could not represent a phase-invariant
      amplitude feature well enough. This is a substantive, negative, architecture-level finding about the linear-functional-first design, and not an
      implementation bug as far as the diagnostics show. The pre-registered rule therefore prevented any KAN-vs-MLP comparison. The prototype
      provides no evidence for or against a KAN advantage.
   4. Consistent with point 3, linear-functional baselines (FPCA) were outperformed by simple summary features on synthetic data. Per-
      channel standard deviation directly carries amplitude information (§10.2). When the risk depended on a non-monotone functional (P-V2), only the
      nonlinear random survival forest moved clearly away from the null. These are descriptive comparisons, not pre-registered tests.
   5. C-MAPSS and PBC baseline results are descriptive and must be read with the caveats in §14. In particular, C-MAPSS contains no natural
      censoring, and the two PBC endpoints estimate different quantities.


R1.14 Limitations, possible leakage, censoring assumptions and unresolved decisions

Scope

      The neural comparisons that motivated the project were not run (D33). All experimental results concern baselines.

Censoring assumptions (D17)

      The AFT likelihood assumes conditionally independent censoring (CA-1).
       Marginal-KM IPCW (IBS, Uno’s C) assumes completely independent censoring (CA-2).
       CA-2 holds by construction for synthetic data and for artificial C-MAPSS censoring.
       For PBC, CA-2 is doubtful. Under E1, transplant (treated as censoring) plausibly depends on disease severity. The conditional-IPCW IBS is a
       sensitivity analysis. It replaces CA-2 with CA-1 plus a correctly specified Cox censoring model, so it is not assumption-free.

C-MAPSS

       No natural censoring. Survival-framing metrics on C-MAPSS are effectively uncensored.
       Artificial censoring (§10.3.3) tests only the code path.
       The data are simulated, and failure is defined by the simulator.
       Option A excludes official test engines shorter than s0.
       Option B reuses engines across landmarks, so windows are correlated. Splits are engine-level (K3), but pooled metrics mix landmarks; per-band
       results are also reported.
       The landmark design decision (D3b) remains unresolved. Both options are reported, and neither is approved as definitive.
       Integer cycles are treated with the continuous approximation (D25).

PBC

       Small sample: 278 at risk at 730 days; about 56 test patients per split.
       Sparse measurements: a median of 3 visits before the landmark (§6). The FPCA representation of such trajectories is weak. Functional modelling
       of PBC at this landmark should be regarded as unreliable.
       Informative observation process: documented by the dataset authors (§10.4.3).
       Endpoint unresolved (D9): E1 and E2 estimate different quantities. Neither is declared definitive. Competing-risks analysis (E3) is not
       implemented, and no competing-risk claims are made.
       Baseline covariates: only age and sex. Treatment arm and other baseline variables were not used.

Possible leakage (checked)

       Splits are by individual or engine (K1, K3).
       Inputs end at the landmark (K4).
       Preprocessing, the censoring KM, FPCA and sensor selection are fitted on training data only (K2).
       Synthetic oracle quantities are isolated (G5, G6, M5).
       The test-set time grids for IBS and the Uno τ use observed test times. This is standard for evaluation and does not affect fitting.
       The synthetic t_max comes from the generator’s pilot sample.

Statistical

       5 replicates or splits give low precision.
       Baseline comparisons are descriptive. No multiplicity-adjusted tests were run.
       STAT tests can fail by chance at their fixed seeds; none failed except R2, which was reproduced deterministically.

Engineering

       Two bugs were found and fixed during the experiments (D36 penalty scaling, D37 constant Cox columns). All affected results were re-run.
       Superseded records are kept and labelled.
       Summary + AFT on C-MAPSS Option A (p ≈ n) often reported converged: false. Its results there are fragile (fit_info).

Literature and status

       No literature review was performed. The prototype is not publication-ready.


R1.15 Reproducibility

          # environment (project-local; never touches the global Python)
          bash scripts/setup_env.sh                          # or: KANFAE_FROM_LOCK=1 bash scripts/setup_env.sh
          bash scripts/verify_env.sh                         # E-1 / E-5 evidence
          # tests (every attempt is appended to reports/logs/test_records.jsonl)
          KANFAE_RUN_ID=rerun .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -rA tests/
          # data (public sources; checksums in reports/run_manifest.json)
          #   C-MAPSS: https://phm-datasets.s3.amazonaws.com/NASA/6.+Turbofan+Engine+Degradation+Simulation+Data+Set.zip
          #            -> extract inner CMAPSSData.zip into data/raw/cmapss/
          #   PBC:     https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/survival_3.8-12.tar.gz -> data/raw/pbc/{DESCRIPTION,data/pbc.rda}
          # experiments (resumable; completed run IDs are skipped)
          bash scripts/run_all_experiments.sh                # synthetic (5 replicates x 6 settings) + C-MAPSS (5 splits)
          .venv/bin/python scripts/run_cmapss.py --splits 5 --analyses cmapss_A,cmapss_A_artificial --models sum_cox --code-version D37
          .venv/bin/python scripts/run_pbc.py --splits 5
          # report
          .venv/bin/python scripts/compile_test_results.py && .venv/bin/python scripts/aggregate_results.py
          .venv/bin/python scripts/make_figures.py && .venv/bin/python scripts/build_report.py
          bash scripts/build_pdf.sh && .venv/bin/python scripts/build_manifest.py


Every executed command, with its exit code and timing, is in reports/logs/commands.jsonl. The full outputs are in reports/logs/*.log. The resumable
narrative log is reports/logs/execution_log.md.
